races.name: Tapestry Events EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Unite John Gillespie Celebration Handicap

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a recent win and second at 5f on Stamford all-weather, but today steps onto soft turf and is technically racing slightly out of natural style at prominent designation; Linda Perratt's yard is 0 from 4 in the last 14 days which is a mild flag, though the horse itself arrives 31 days fresh and has strong place claims if able to dictate unchallenged.

runners_data.name: King Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Trainer Easterby duo are 2 from 35 in 14 days but the horse won last time at 5f on good ground and has placed on similar going before; prominent style suits this race shape perfectly and Billy Garritty is a reliable handler of 5f speed handicaps — the most natural tactical fit behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who placed twice at 5f on good and once on Stamford, showing he handles cut in the ground; the blinkers are on, Lewis Edmunds takes the ride for in-form Dods yard (3 from 23 in 14 days), but needing to make ground from the rear on a flat track with a congested midfield is a challenge.

runners_data.name: Auntie Jo
runners_data.note: Won last time at 5f on Stamford and placed at 5f on good for O'Meara who is notably active (5 from 48 in 14 days); prominent style fits the race shape well and the hood is retained — a serious contender in the tracking position if she can hold that spot against King Of The Jungle.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Won twice recently at 5f on good, both close home, and the hood (headgear h) is in place for Jim Goldie whose stable is in strong form (7 from 41 in 14 days); though a hold-up type, her natural finishing kick gives her relevance if the soft ground brings the field back to her — the most credible of the closers on raw form.

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who ran on soft last time (8th at 7f) and has limited form at the trip, with Gary Harrison's yard only 1 from 3 in 14 days; hold-up style on a flat 5f soft with a compressed field makes his task harder, and the form string shows no win or place at the distance.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural style is at the rear, repositioned to midfield on the map purely because the field is saturated with back-markers; the trainer Smith yard is 0 from 7 in 14 days, recent form reads 80-763, and soft-ground form at 5f shows just one placing in 15 — very hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine has two from 17 in the 14-day window but this three-year-old has a noted tendency to fade in the finish and is a true hold-up type shown in midfield only because too many closers cannot all sit at the rear; 48 days off and limited soft-ground form compound the concerns.

runners_data.name: Regal Dream
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan is 3 from 25 recently but the horse has finished 11th and 10th in its last two starts on Stamford, and a 61-day layoff adds uncertainty; a natural back-marker shown in midfield due to field saturation, the blinkers are on but the form gives very little encouragement on soft ground.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on good two starts ago (the best recent piece of form for a hold-up horse in this cluster) and the Mike Smith yard has two from 18 in 14 days; arriving only 5 days after a run, recovery must be considered — a true rear-runner mapped forward because of redistribution, carrying a style-fit discount.

runners_data.name: Bonito Cavalo
runners_data.note: Goldie's second runner in this race alongside Wee Mary, a seven-year-old with a fading-in-finish flag and a form string of 0-0879 suggesting very modest current level; another genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map, carrying 68 days off and all four recent runs on Stamford rather than soft turf — hard to recommend.

races.paceDynamic: Henery Hawk is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press for early supremacy, is expected to stride into a comfortable lead from the gates and control tempo throughout this 5f soft-ground sprint. King Of The Jungle and Auntie Jo are the likeliest prominent-tracking types to sit closest behind, meaning the pace will be steady-to-sustainable rather than frantic — a tempo that gives the leader every chance to conserve energy for the closing stages. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Supremissy, Regal Dream, Royal Duke, Ski Angel and Bonito Cavalo are all true hold-up horses crowded into a midfield that is likely to become congested on soft ground, reducing their ability to produce late runs from their natural position. On this race shape — lone leader dictating on a flat, soft-ground 5f with a compressed midfield and no pressure from off the pace — the profile that benefits most is prominent-tracking types who can sit just off Henery Hawk and pounce in the final furlong without needing to make up large amounts of ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader controls, trackers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Henery Hawk sets a sustainable solo gallop and prominent-seated horses track closely enough to challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Henery Hawk sets a sustainable solo gallop and prominent-seated horses track closely enough to challenge inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader holds on unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and the prominent-trackers fail to close, leaving Henery Hawk to score wire-to-wire.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely moderate and the prominent-trackers fail to close, leaving Henery Hawk to score wire-to-wire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up closers get home late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens enough to leave Henery Hawk vulnerable and a clear rail or stands-side lane opens for late-finishing types.
scenarios.body: If the early pace quickens enough to leave Henery Hawk vulnerable and a clear rail or stands-side lane opens for late-finishing types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic sprint, pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses break sharply and contest the lead, turning the race into a competitive burn-up that leaves the front group exposed late.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses break sharply and contest the lead, turning the race into a competitive burn-up that leaves the front group exposed late.

watchPoints.text: Henery Hawk's ability to dictate solo sets the whole race — watch whether he is allowed a soft lead from the gates or if King Of The Jungle or Auntie Jo press him early, as any significant early pressure on soft ground could fundamentally change the outcome.

King Of The Jungle and Auntie Jo are both seeking the same prominent tracking position directly behind Henery Hawk — if both attempt to sit there simultaneously, a scrimmage for that berth in the first furlong could compromise one or both and hand a positional advantage to the other.

Wee Mary's last two wins both came at 5f on good ground for a stable firing on all cylinders — monitor market moves here as she is the hold-up horse most likely to defy the congested rear-field problem if the soft ground slows the pace enough to bring closers into play.

The large cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Supremissy, Regal Dream, Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Bonito Cavalo) will likely bunch together in the middle to rear of the field — watch for traffic issues and interference in the straight that could flatter or compromise several of these runners' finishing positions.

Going confirmation is soft throughout the Ayr card — the 2:18 race is explicitly logged as Soft at 5f, so any further deterioration during the afternoon could increase the premium on prominent-held positions and further penalise horses needing a clear run from the rear.

races.name: Unite Natalie Egan Celebration Handicap (For The Johnstone Rose Bowl) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Albany
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who should get a clear lead at a sustainable pace; soft going is fine for her but she is racing out of her natural lead role into a prominent map position — take that with a pinch of salt as she is the most likely pace-setter here; 289 days off is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Square Necker
runners_data.note: In excellent current form (1-2-1 in recent runs), trainer Philippart De Foy in 1/17 form over 14 days, and has soft-ground experience; a natural prominent racer who should secure a comfortable tracking position behind Albany and this is a career-best opportunity at this trip.

runners_data.name: Dancingwithmyself
runners_data.note: Has won twice on soft/yielding ground at 14f and clearly handles this type of test well, making him one of the most relevant soft-ground profiles in the field; Michael Bell yard in 1/19 recent form but the horse's own going record is the key selling point here.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has struggled for form lately (0-0-0-8-7 recent figures), and soft-ground form over this trip is limited to mid-field finishes; needs something to go wrong for the prominent horses and even then this looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Peaky Blinder
runners_data.note: Has won on soft and at 14f, making the combination here highly relevant; Andrew Balding yard in strong 9/63 form and Jason Hart takes the ride, with the headgear (p) adding a small variable — one of the stronger profiles for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: Sharp form recently includes a second at 12f on good, but his soft-going runs are a touch disappointing and this trip at 1m5f is further than his best work; pushed to midfield on the pace map because too many prominent types compete for that position in this field — his in-running position may be compromised.

runners_data.name: Boatswain
runners_data.note: Ran at 14f on soft without threatening and the step to 1m5f is a query; Simon and Ed Crisford yard ticking over at 1/20 recently, and as a horse who wants to race prominently but is unlikely to secure that berth here, he faces an awkward profile in this shape.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has respectable form at 14-16f on good ground; soft ground is an unknown for him given his form string is almost entirely on good surfaces, which is the main concern given conditions today at Ayr.

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: Racing for William Haggas who is in excellent 11/53 form, but this horse's best work has come over shorter trips (8-10f) and on good ground — stepping up to 1m5f on soft is a significant double question mark; as a horse who wants to race prominently, he is unlikely to get that position and may lack the stamina for this test anyway.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: Two wins in recent form (1-1-3-5-7 shape), hold-up operator who has placed on soft before; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is useful at the weights and Jim Goldie's yard is firing — needs a truly run race to get competitive but the form uptick is noteworthy.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Another Jim Goldie runner with Amie Waugh's 3lb claim; ran just 7 days ago and form figures show consistent placing rather than winning — hold-up style needs the pace to be genuine and the run back quickly on soft ground is a small concern.

runners_data.name: Alba Chiara
runners_data.note: Best form came at 13-18f on good ground, including a win at 18f; trainer's yard is quiet at 0/8 over 14 days and recent form is patchy (0-0-2-1-1 reversed); hold-up style at a long trip on soft could theoretically suit but the form and stable form are against her.

races.paceDynamic: Albany is the one confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine pace rival likely to press from the outset on soft ground over 1m5f, she should be able to dictate at a sustainable, even tempo from the front. Square Necker, Dancingwithmyself, Peaky Blinder, and Pole Star are all genuine prominent racers who will contest the positions immediately behind, creating a settled but organised gallop rather than a frantically run race. The field does hold more prominent-minded types than the shape can comfortably accommodate — Boatswain, Ashnak, and Divine Knight are true prominent runners who have been pushed into the midfield map because Albany and the other prominent horses will crowd them out, meaning those three will either have to race further back than ideal or expend energy getting to their preferred position. This shape — a lone leader setting a controlled pace with a bunch of prominent horses tracking — strongly favours genuine prominent types with soft-ground credentials, particularly those who can sit in a perfect stalking position and produce a sustained gallop home rather than a sharp turn of foot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Albany Controls, Prominent Track
scenarios.trigger: If Albany leads at a measured tempo and the prominent stalkers settle into a rhythm behind without incident.
scenarios.body: If Albany leads at a measured tempo and the prominent stalkers settle into a rhythm behind without incident.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds Them Out
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going deteriorates further and the race becomes a true stamina test from halfway.
scenarios.body: If the soft going deteriorates further and the race becomes a true stamina test from halfway.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough that the field strings out and a late finisher can make ground from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely honest enough that the field strings out and a late finisher can make ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Crowding Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types jostles for position early and one or more of the redistributed horses burns energy forcing their way up.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of prominent types jostles for position early and one or more of the redistributed horses burns energy forcing their way up.

watchPoints.text: Albany's 289-day absence is the single biggest risk to the dominant scenario — if she fades before the home turn having led, the race opens up entirely for those tracking her.

Boatswain, Ashnak, and Divine Knight are all natural prominent horses who cannot all get their preferred position; watch for early scrimmaging or energy-wasting as they jostle behind Albany in the first half mile on soft ground.
Pole Star has raced almost exclusively on good ground and the step onto soft at Ayr today is an untested variable for him — if conditions are worse than expected he may not fire.

Letsbefrank has won two of his last three starts and carries a 5lb claim — worth monitoring in-running as a horse whose form has genuinely turned around even if the style requires things to set up favourably.

Square Necker is 1 from 4 on soft ground and the trainer's 1/17 14-day record suggests the yard is not firing at full capacity — confirmation of how well he handles today's conditions in the early stages will be key.

races.name: Dalcon Civil Engineering Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Showed soft-ground form with a win over 6f on soft and a placed effort, and drops into this 7f classified stakes in fair shape 12 days fresh; true hold-up runner who needs to find daylight in a compressed finish, and the step to 7f soft is the key query.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Ran just four days ago and showed a win and placed effort at 7f-8f on good ground, though soft form is minimal; David Allan takes the mount for Tim Easterby and at age 3 this horse's stamina for 7f soft is unproven but the yard is in solid form.

runners_data.name: Queenies Pal
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap applied and has a placed run on soft over 6f; in reality a true hold-up horse, though the crowded rear means it may have to race closer than ideal — that role reversal tempers confidence despite the going fitness.

runners_data.name: Royal Baroness
runners_data.note: Modest form with soft-ground experience but no wins and a tendency to post mid-table finishes; genuinely needs to race from behind, yet with the rear wall congested, Rhys Elliott faces a difficult tactical puzzle — discount accordingly.

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.note: Carries a 3lb claimer advantage via Amie Waugh but soft-ground record is thin and form over 7f is limited; runs 23 days fresh and while the 7f trip at Ayr could suit, the lack of soft-going evidence is a clear concern.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: A veteran at 9 years old with placed efforts over 7f in similar conditions including two second-place finishes on this trip; in reality prefers to close from off the pace and soft ground suits the grinding style — Michael & David Easterby send this in form.

runners_data.name: Trais Fluors
runners_data.note: Remarkable 12-year-old running for Linda Perratt whose recent form figures are uninspiring; 18 days since last run and no recent win to speak of, making this a tough ask even if the hold-up style loosely fits a sprint-finish scenario.

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Garden
runners_data.note: Tagged as prone to fading in the finish, which is a serious flag in a soft-ground sprint — even if the field is slow early, this horse's tendency to weaken late makes a compressed finish the worst scenario; Jason Hart cannot overcome that profile flaw.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Ran yesterday, just one day since last race, which is an almost unprecedented turnaround and the primary story here; Jim Goldie sends it out again and the soft-ground record is limited, making the fitness and recovery question dominant regardless of style.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Consistent soft and good-to-soft form with multiple placed efforts over 7f, including two second and two third-place finishes at this trip; a genuine hold-up horse that may find itself racing in midfield due to field congestion, but the proven record in similar conditions gives it solid claims in any compressed finish.

runners_data.name: No Nay Nevermind
runners_data.note: Ran six times recently with modest figures and soft-ground form is limited to one placed run from a small sample; Iain Jardine's yard has runners but this horse's form string over 7f does not inspire, and being nudged out of its natural position weakens the profile further.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: Has posted a string of fourth-place finishes without converting, suggesting a horse that runs consistently but cannot quite find the extra gear to win; soft-ground form is minimal from a small sample, and the habit of running into places without winning is a concern.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field, there is no horse likely to dominate from the front and dictate a true pace — the early fractions on soft ground over 7f at Ayr will almost certainly be moderate, drifting into a messy sprint-finish from the home turn. Every single runner carries a hold-up or midfield style tag, meaning the entire field is pointing at the same patch of real estate late in the race, and there is nobody to stretch the field out in the early stages. Soft ground compounds this: without a genuine pace-setter to lean on, horses will bunch in the final two furlongs and the outcome will hinge on who can produce the sharpest late surge from a compressed group. This race shape heavily favours horses with a proven ability to quicken in soft conditions from just off a slow pace — specifically those with the cleanest soft-ground record, strongest recent form, and a jockey with enough race-craft to find daylight in a wall of horses. The field holds substantially more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear; Queenies Pal, Monhammer, No Nay Nevermind, Approaching Dawn, Evelyn's Garden, Pebble Dash and Ring Of Gold are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map, and in reality several must race closer than ideal — those drawn widest or with the most natural toe are likeliest to press forward and accidentally make the pace.

scenarios.title: Crawl Turns Into Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If no horse asserts early and the field bunches throughout, producing a compressed sprint finish from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: If no horse asserts early and the field bunches throughout, producing a compressed sprint finish from the 2f pole.

scenarios.title: Accidentally Honest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one or two of the redistributed hold-up horses are pushed forward by jockeys seeking position, creating a slightly more genuine tempo.
scenarios.body: If one or two of the redistributed hold-up horses are pushed forward by jockeys seeking position, creating a slightly more genuine tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Dictates Shape
scenarios.trigger: If horses drawn high use the soft ground to track widest and effectively control the pace lane, fragmenting the field.
scenarios.body: If horses drawn high use the soft ground to track widest and effectively control the pace lane, fragmenting the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the going rides testing rather than merely soft and stamina separates the field from the 3f mark onward.
scenarios.body: If the going rides testing rather than merely soft and stamina separates the field from the 3f mark onward.

watchPoints.text: Approaching Dawn ran just one day ago — monitor pre-race for any signs of fatigue or stiffness that would make it a non-runner or a false price, as that turnaround is extreme even for a handicap yard operating in form.

With no front-runner confirmed and every runner holding a hold-up style, watch for a chaotic break where multiple jockeys attempt to track wide to find cleaner ground — a fierce scrimmage for position from the off could cause interference in the opening furlong.

Monhammer's soft-ground placed record over 7f makes it the most likely beneficiary of a slow-run sprint finish, but Paul Mulrennan will need to thread through a genuine wall of horses — watch for the draw and any wide passage it can exploit.

Evelyn's Garden is flagged as fading in the finish and soft ground over 7f will only magnify that tendency — if the pace is predictably slow and the run-in tests stamina, this horse could drop away sharply and cause trouble for runners immediately behind.

Ring Of Gold at 9 years old has soft-ground form and a pair of placed runs over 7f that make it quietly interesting, but Billy Garritty must navigate from a congested hold-up position — watch whether it gets a clear run or is bottled up at a critical stage.

races.name: Unite George Ramsay Celebration EBF Land O'Burns Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Beautiful Diamond
runners_data.note: Listed-class front-runner who has won on soft ground and is dropped back to 5f where she is most effective; uncontested lead is the key — Burke and Sam James will use that asset aggressively, and her style-fit score reflects she is nudged into a lead role she naturally suits here rather than her usual prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Billie Be Quick
runners_data.note: The only true hold-up horse in the race, but all five recent runs have been on good or faster ground, leaving her soft-ground credentials completely unknown; Mulrennan will need significant pace collapse ahead of her, and her last two runs over 6f on good suggest the drop to 5f soft is a demanding ask of her stamina.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good for Bethell and is a genuine front-of-the-field type, but with so many prominent rivals entered this race compresses her into a midfield slot on the map; Oisin Orr will likely push forward regardless, though the resultant jostling for position could cost her energy on a soft surface.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained filly with a sharp 5f win on good and placed on soft, making her one of the more versatile going profiles in this field; she is a natural pace-setter pushed into the prominent-but-squeezed group, and if Harry Davies can manoeuvre her onto Beautiful Diamond's quarters from a clean draw she has the raw ability to challenge.

runners_data.name: Layla Liz
runners_data.note: Three wins on standard Tapeta at Southwell suggest an all-weather specialist; her soft-turf form is sparse (one run, 10th on good) and the surface here is a significant query, even though Andrew Mullen rides and Watson's yard is in reasonable form — she appears here in the hold-up zone only because the model has redistributed her from a naturally prominent position.

runners_data.name: Luna A Inbhir Nis
runners_data.note: Local Scottish trainer Katie Scott represents with a filly that has finished third or second in similar company on soft and good; her prominent style suits a race run at this tempo, though her OR of 96 and the 0-from-15 record on similar going for the profile type is a caution against overrating her chances.

runners_data.name: Rhyme Dust
runners_data.note: Beckett's 4-year-old has contested 6f races almost exclusively and drops to the minimum trip on soft — a potentially unflattering combination given she has no win in recent form and her soft-ground record reads 0W1P from three efforts; Hector Crouch's booking gives modest confidence but the profile is workmanlike rather than exciting.

runners_data.name: Rose Of Honour
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts including two on standard Tapeta at Southwell, but this is a very different test — Listed class on soft turf over 5f against seasoned rivals; Tate's filly has never raced in these conditions and her inexperience on cut ground is a real unknown, though her natural prominence and winning mentality are compelling if she handles the surface.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Princess
runners_data.note: Lyons-trained 3-year-old who hasn't run for 250 days — an eyecatcher for a yard that can produce them fresh, but the layoff combined with a drop to 5f on soft turf and a compressed prominent group she cannot fully access is a significant collection of risks; her best form is over 6-7f on standard and good.

runners_data.name: Argentine Tango
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3-year-old has placed on soft before but recent form reads 4-4-6-6-7 and the horse has failed to land a blow in similar company consistently; David Allan's experience around Ayr is genuine, though dropping into this company on soft ground looks more of a fitness or handicap exercise than a winning opportunity.

runners_data.name: Cardiff By The Sea
runners_data.note: Stack's 3-year-old won over 5f on soft at the Curragh and is one of the strongest soft-ground credentials in the field; she is a genuine prominent racer forced into the midfield slot on the map by competition for position, and Slattery will push forward — if she secures a berth handy to the pace her chance is better than her OR of 91 implies.

runners_data.name: Coconut Cove
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3-year-old won over 6f on standard and placed on soft, but the drop to 5f looks a slight trip concern given her pedigree and best efforts have come at the longer distance; Jack Mitchell is a polished jockey and she wears a hood, which often sharpens Varian's types, but the trip is a genuine query.

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby youngster with back-to-back wins on standard ground, taking the step up to Listed level on soft turf — an ambitious move, and the horse sits naturally in the prominent cluster even though the map places her in the compressed midfield group; Garritty rides, and the yard has 3 from 30 over 14 days, giving limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Thenandnow
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on soft at Carlisle and has consistent form in that ground — the surface here is her best chance of outperforming her OR of 81 in Listed class; she is a natural front-runner shuffled back by the density of pace rivals, and if the soft ground genuinely tests the field's stamina she becomes a sneaky value proposition.

runners_data.name: Thora
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 3-year-old won over 6f on standard Tapeta but has a soft-ground run to her name and has had 104 days off the track — Ryan can place a horse fresh but this is a significant step in class; Tom Eaves takes over and she is another true prominent type competing for a lead position she is unlikely to secure at the flag.

races.paceDynamic: Beautiful Diamond is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead on comparable pace credentials, she should settle into a controlled, uncontested gallop from the off — soft ground will steady the tempo further, making this a sit-and-sprint affair rather than a true test of stamina. The field is saturated with prominent-types: Kinswoman, Cardiff By The Sea, Fluorescence, Sapphire Princess, Thora, Shes Got A Brother and Thenandnow are all natural front-of-the-field racers who cannot all occupy their preferred berths, meaning a congested, hustling pack will form just off Beautiful Diamond, with several forced wider or deeper than they'd like. This compression of the prominent group on soft ground over 5f creates a scenario where the pace is genuinely sustainable — not truly slow, but metronomic enough that the leader holds a meaningful positional advantage into the final furlong. The race shape overwhelmingly favours horses that can secure a prominent pitch early and travel within themselves, rather than late-closers, since there are almost no genuine hold-up types in the field to generate a finishing kick from the rear — Billie Be Quick is the sole authentic hold-up runner, and Layla Liz is a redistributed prominent type rather than a true closer.

scenarios.body: If Beautiful Diamond dictates an honest but unforced gallop on soft and the overcrowded prominent pack cannot properly mount a coordinated challenge.

scenarios.body: If the congested group immediately behind Beautiful Diamond travels smoothly and one breaks clear entering the final furlong to gun down a tiring leader.

scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely testing in the soft conditions and the field spreads across the track, turning the final 2f into a war of attrition.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely testing in the soft conditions and the field spreads across the track, turning the final 2f into a war of attrition.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses badly in the final furlong and the one genuine hold-up runner, Billie Be Quick, finds a gap on the outside late.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses badly in the final furlong and the one genuine hold-up runner, Billie Be Quick, finds a gap on the outside late.

watchPoints.text: Cardiff By The Sea and Kinswoman are both natural front-runners who will push for the prominent positions hard at the start — watch for an early jostle 2-3f out that burns off rivals on soft ground, potentially gifting Beautiful Diamond a free lead.

Rose Of Honour is unbeaten but has never faced soft ground in her three-start career — if the going visibly rides very testing in the 4:08 slot, monitor her early action to see whether she is travelling or toiling, as her market position may be built entirely on all-weather form.

Sapphire Princess has been off for 250 days and is stepping into Listed class on a surface she hasn't proven on — a slow jump or sluggish early move from Sheehy would confirm she needs the run, making her a horse to watch rather than back.

Beautiful Diamond's draw and ability to find clean rail ground will be critical — if she is forced wide early by the pack pressing from her outside, the sustainable-pace advantage that makes her the map's pivotal horse is significantly reduced.

Billie Be Quick is the only genuine hold-up horse and her finishing effort over the final furlong will reveal whether the pace was truly honest — if she makes significant ground late it signals that the race was run fast enough to bring closers into play, which recalibrates how to read the next race on the card.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner soft-ground 7f handicap and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to pressurise him — he can roll along at a sustainable gallop and dictate terms throughout. The soft going at Ayr today will stretch the field out early, rewarding anything that travels smoothly into the race rather than those who need to be produced with a late surge on tired ground. The field carries far more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate: Circle Of Trust, Ellie's de Vega, Sanny Doo, Horace Wallace, and Blue Mantle are all natural hold-up types redistributed to mapped midfield positions because they cannot all secure the rear berths their style demands — the most likely to find genuine cover are Horace Wallace (Oisin Orr, experienced handler) and Blue Mantle (Andrew Mullen, proven soft-ground runner). With one unhurried pace-setter and a field that is structurally overcrowded at the back, this race shape favours prominent or at-the-pace horses who can track Napolian without burning energy and quicken at the two-pole — not true closers, who face the twin problems of soft ground sapping their finishing kick and a muddling gallop that may not set up a genuine late run.

watchPoints.text: Magistery is the only horse in the field with a win on soft ground and four soft-ground runs to draw on — if Dods has him ready off 30 days, he is the most obvious beneficiary of an uncontested Napolian gallop.|

Napolian has only one soft-ground run in his last five and steps up from 6f to 7f — if the going tests his stamina, the race could unravel from the front earlier than expected and compress the field.|

Blue Mantle and Horace Wallace are both genuine hold-up horses who cannot all secure the rear berths they need — watch how Orr and Mullen position them in the first furlong, as their chance depends entirely on finding cover that may not exist.|

Milford Grange has placed in two of three soft-ground runs and Billy Garritty will be looking to track Napolian off the pace — his 7f stamina on soft is unproven but his consistency in this going band is the clearest form line in the race.|

Real Jack's unquantified style is a genuine tactical wildcard — if Mulrennan pushes him forward early, he could either help set a stronger gallop that disadvantages Napolian or simply fade out of contention on soft ground where he has no proven form.|

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Sunshine is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner soft-ground handicap and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival — Parisiac has prominent tendencies but is a 5f specialist stepping up in trip, meaning Eternal Sunshine can dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop from the front. With soft ground at Ayr slowing the tempo further, she is likely to roll along at a comfortable, sustainable pace rather than being asked to burn excessively, giving her every chance to dictate the fractions and dominate the key rail positions. The field behind is overwhelmingly stacked with hold-up types, and with Aberama Gold, Oriental Prince, Abduction, Dandy Magic, Lion's House, Kelpie Grey, Whiskey Kisses and Falcon Queen all redistributed out of their natural rear positions into midfield slots on the map, the true closers cannot all reach the rear of the field naturally — many will be racing closer than ideal, compromising their ability to produce a genuine late finish. This race shape strongly favours a confirmed front-runner who can control the pace on soft ground without being pressed, or at worst a prominent racer able to track the leader closely from early and pounce in the home straight.

watchPoints.text: Eternal Sunshine — watch her away from the stalls; if she breaks cleanly and crosses to the rail uncontested, the race may effectively be over early as no other confirmed front-runner will go with her.

Parisiac — monitor at the 2f pole; if she has enough petrol after stepping up from 5f and sits just off Eternal Sunshine, she could prove a major threat given her two soft-ground wins, but her finishing effort may flatten out at the longer trip.
Roberto Caro — watch for a position switch entering the final 2f; his soft-ground win and multiple placings in similar conditions make him the standout closer if he can find a gap from midfield.
Dandy Magic — keep an eye on the draw and early positioning; returning from a long break, a clean passage from midfield on soft ground is the one scenario that brings his going record into play.

Field width at the 4f mark — in a 14-runner soft-ground sprint at Ayr, early crowding and horses losing positions is a genuine risk; any horse caught in traffic at that stage will have its chance ended on this ground.
